text: When you work with APIs, you are essentially asking a remote server for data or asking it to perform an action. This involves sending HTTP requests, like GET to retrieve information or POST to send new data. Most modern APIs return their results in JSON format, which is easy for both humans and machines to read. To access private data, you usually need authentication, often using an API key or a token. Remember that APIs often have rate limits, meaning you can only make a certain number of requests within a specific time period. Finally, always include error handling in your code. This way, if a request fails or the server returns an error, your program can react gracefully instead of crashing.
